Proposition 2.2. Let V ‡ {0} be an ordered normed space whose cone has an interior point v. Then v is an order unit and the order unit norm || || is weaker than the original norm || || on V. Moreover, every positive functional on V is continuous with respect to both norms.

Note that the two norms in Proposition 2.2 need not be equivalent, see, e.g., [6, Example 1.5.12|. For a detailed discussion in ordered Banach spaces, see |4, Proposition 2.11]. For an ordered vector space (V, V+), a set S' of positive linear functionals from V to R is said to determine positivity if, for every v € V, one has v ≥ 0 if p(v) ≥ O for all « € S'. Note that, if V is an order unit space and I C V+ is given as in (2.1), then ext ≥ determines positivity. We will make use of the following two simple propositions.

Proposition 2.3. Let X be an ordered normed vector space and let S' I X+. The following are equivalent:

(i) The set S' determines positivity, i.e., for every x € X, the inequality (x', x) ≥ 0 for all x' E S' implies that x ≥ O. (ii) The positive-linear hull of S' is weak-* dense in the dual wedge X4. Proof. "(i) → (ii)" We show the contraposition. Let C' C X4 denote the weak-* closure of the positive-linear hull of S' and assume that there exists a point xo € X+ that is not in Ci. By the Hahn-Banach separation theorem in the locally convex space X' with the weak-* topology, there exists a weak-* continuous functional x": X' → R and a number y € R such that (x", x') ≥ Y > (x", x) for all x' € C". Due to the weak-* continuity of x", there exists an element x € X such that x" is the point evaluation at x, see [13, § IV.1.2 on pp. 124-125]. It follows that (x, x') ≥ Y > (x, x) for all x' € C'. Since 0 € C, we obtain y ≤ 0. Therefore, x is not in X+. As C' is a wedge, for every x' € C' we have (x, x') ≥ 0, hence C' does not determine positivity. "(ii) → (i)" If x € X satisfies (x', x) ≥ 0 for all x' € S', then it follows from (ii) that the same inequality holds for all x' € X4. As X+ is closed, this implies that x € X+. • The following is a primal version of Proposition 2.3. As its proof is similar, we omit it. Proposition 2.4.
